text:
Carmen S: Hydra POC with Orchestr — FYI they're seeing inconsistent TTFT. Some requests 1.2s first-token, others ~350ms. Also intermittent 429s under burst. Customer wants go/no-go by Friday. Can eng/runtime + SRE help triage? Main asks: 1) quick batching/cache tweaks to improve TTFT, 2) explain/mitigate 429s, 3) rough pricing for Dedicated if we push them that route.

Jamal R: Uploading a sample request log now and a short repro script. @Priya M are you able to look at model routing + batch windows? They reported chat-style requests with a large system prompt.

Priya M: Got the logs. Pattern is chat with a ~1.5k token system prompt then short user messages. That explains high variance — prefix cache misses on many sessions. Recs: enable prefix_cache for their route, lower `max_new_tokens` during load tests, and set `batch_latency_ms` to 12ms for that model. Also, if they use streaming, use `stream_chunk_size=64` to let first token bridge faster.

Priya M: Example route override we can push temporarily:
```json
{
  "route": "orchestr-prod-poc",
  "prefix_cache": true,
  "batch_latency_ms": 12,
  "stream_chunk_size": 64,
  "max_new_tokens": 128
}
```

Marco L: 429s are from the swarm throttler on our side — they're hitting the burst cap when many parallel users hit cold prefixes. We can bump burst_window for their account to 2x for the trial window (24h) while they run the test. Also confirm client retry headers; they should use exponential backoff (recommended base 200ms, max 2s).

Elise K: I uploaded full request+response traces + a few request_ids to the shared support bucket: s3://redwood-support/poc/orchestr/1823456789/. Included the runbook for how to toggle `prefix_cache` for the route.

Jamal R: Customer is running their load generator at ~120 RPS with 8 concurrent clients. Most cold sessions are coming from different conversation IDs (no reuse). If they can reuse conversation/session ids we'll see much better cache hit rate. I pinged them to change generator to reuse sessions for next run.

Raj P: For Dedicated discussion: we'll need to start the security questionnaire ASAP. Orchestr flagged data residency and KMS/HSM. For short-term trial we can offer VPC endpoints + envelope encryption with our KMS integration. I'll DM the questionnaire template to Carmen.

Dana T: Pricing notes for AE: ballpark for a small dedicated pool that hits 100 RPS ~ $30k–60k/mo depending on GPU class and committed utilization. For the POC trial we can offer a time-limited uplift credit if they convert in 30 days. Will confirm exact numbers after we know target steady-state throughput.

deploy-bot: deploy 2024-06-10T15:04:12Z: pushed route override `orchestr-prod-poc` -> prefix_cache=true, batch_latency_ms=12 (change id: dpl-8392).

Priya M: I applied the route override to their route in staging and saw median TTFT drop from ~700ms to ~260ms in our test harness when reusing conversation ids. Cold-new-conversation TTFT still ~480ms, but much more stable.

Marco L: Burst cap lifted for their account until 2024-06-11T16:00Z. Monitor for 429s and let me know request_ids for any new 429s.

Carmen S: Perfect — quick plan: 1) Jamal will coordinate with customer to reuse session ids and run 2 stress windows (low/high). 2) Priya keep the route override in place and share telemetry. 3) Marco monitor throttles and revert cap after window. 4) Raj send security questionnaire. 5) Dana follow up on formal pricing. ETA: initial results by EOD today. @everyone :thumbsup:

Jamal R: On it — I'll schedule a short joint test at 18:00 PT and send a join link to Orchestr and the SWARM channel.

Elise K: If anything else breaks, add the request_id and I'll fetch full traces.

Priya M: Also note: if they expect many unique conversation namespaces, we should suggest a small client-side sticky conversation id (guid) per user to improve cache locality. That's an easy SDK change.

Dana T: I'll prep an interim pricing slide and send to Carmen for customer-facing call.

Carmen S: Thanks team — will update the customer and loop back once Jamal has the test results.
